program_name: Bachelor in Food and Enogastronomy Sciences (IT: Laurea in Scienze alimentari ed enogastronomiche; DE: Bachelor in Lebensmittelwissenschaften, Önologie und Gastronomie)
teaching_language: Trilingual (English / Italian / German). The 'At a glance' box states: 'Courses will be taught in English, Italian and German (trilingual)'. Per-course language tags in the official L-26 course-description PDF give the following credit weighting: YEAR 1 (63 CP, identical for both majors) is English-leaning — English 37 CP (Elements of Mathematics and Statistics 8; Principles of General, Organic and Biological Chemistry 9; Plant Biodiversity and Sustainable Cultivation Methods 12; Biology of Microorganisms and Secondary Metabolites 8), German 20 CP (Sustainable Management and Environmental Impact of Livestock Production Systems 8; Physics and Computer Science 6; Food Systems 6), Italian 6 CP (Agri-food Marketing and Law). YEAR 2 flips to Italian-dominant: in the Food Technology major Italian 30 CP, English 9 CP, German 9 CP (plus 12 CP language-neutral free choice/internship); in the Enogastronomy major Italian 30 CP, German 16 CP, English 3 CP (plus 6 CP internship). YEAR 3: Food Technology English 12 / Italian 9 / German 12; Enogastronomy English 18 / Italian 9 / German 12. WHOLE-DEGREE TOTALS: Food Technology major — English 58 CP, Italian 45 CP, German 41 CP, language-neutral 36 CP (free choice, internships, thesis, transversal skills); Enogastronomy major — English 58 CP, Italian 45 CP, German 48 CP, language-neutral 29 CP. English is therefore the single largest language but only about one third of the degree, and there is NO English-only pathway: German is compulsory from the first semester of year 1 and Italian becomes the dominant language of year 2. A compulsory 3 CP 'Specialised Language (English)' course (B2/B2+ level) sits in year 2 of both majors. [uncertain] — the credit split is reconstructed from the per-module language tags in the L-26 course-description PDF (dated 01.02.2025); one module (Sustainable cultivation methods and quality of products for food processing) is tagged 3 credits in that PDF but 6 CP in the 2026/27 brochure study plan.
campus: Bozen-Bolzano (main city campus, Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano). Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences. The 'At a glance' box states simply 'Campus: Bozen-Bolzano'. Practical teaching also uses the Faculty's food laboratories and Kitchen Lab at NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano, and the programme runs eno-gastronomy workshops off campus in Merano (Castel Fragsburg, Palace Meran) plus excursions and study trips. Not Brixen-Bressanone, Bruneck-Brunico, Trento or Innsbruck.
degree_class: L-26 (Scienze e tecnologie agro-alimentari / Agro-food Sciences and Technologies). 180 ECTS, 3 years.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered and actively recruiting. Both the Early Bird and the Late ranking lists for 2026/27 have been published and filled (27 + 22 EU admitted, 1 non-EU admitted). Critically, at the verification date the ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION IS STILL OPEN for this programme: unibz's additional-application-session page lists 'Food and Enogastronomy Sciences' among the bachelor programmes accepting applications from 18/08/2026 to 04/09/2026 (EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only), with studies starting in October 2026.
is_new_programme: Recent, but not brand new. The current name and study plan date from academic year 2025/26 — the first cohort under the name 'Food and Enogastronomy Sciences' / 'Scienze alimentari ed enogastronomiche' is 'coorte 2025' (confirmed by the Municipality of Meran-Merano scholarship call, which is addressed to 'studenti e studentesse della laurea in Scienze alimentari ed enogastronomiche (L-26) iscritti al primo anno nell'a.a 2025-26, coorte 2025'). 2026/27 is therefore the SECOND intake under this name. The programme is a renamed and restructured continuation of the former 'Bachelor in Enogastronomy in Mountain Areas' / 'Scienze enogastronomiche di montagna', launched by unibz together with three-Michelin-star chef Norbert Niederkofler and announced in a unibz news item dated 22/03/2022: the old programme URL (…/bachelor-enogastronomy-mountain-areas) now resolves to this programme's page, and the site keeps a separate 'course offering 2022' page for students 'Enrolled before 2025'. [uncertain] — unibz does not state the rename explicitly in English; this is inferred from the URL redirect, the legacy course-offering page and the 'coorte 2025' wording.
majors_tracks_study_plans: Common first year (63 CP: mathematics and statistics, chemistry, biology/microbiology, physics and computer science, livestock systems, plant biodiversity, food systems, agri-food marketing and law), then TWO majors chosen from the second year: (1) MAJOR FOOD TECHNOLOGY — focus on production processes, quality control and food safety; year 2 adds Plant Genetics (3), Measurements and Controls (6), Unit Operations (6), Instrumental Analytical Techniques (6); year 3 adds Bioprocesses and Thermodynamics (9), Post-harvest Technologies (6), Protection of Stored Products (6). (2) MAJOR ENOGASTRONOMY — focus on valorisation of local food and wine production; year 2 adds Geography of Food and Sustainable Regional Development (3), Food Anthropology (6), Seminar 'Cook the Mountain' (7), Food Design and Immersive Food Related Experiences (6); year 3 adds Management of Food Processes (9), Business Organization (6), Microbial Fermentations in Gastronomy (6). Both majors share Hygiene, Food Microbiology and Food Industries (12), Advanced Enology and Enography (6), Nutrition Physiology (6), Specialised Language English (3), Food Quality Evaluation (12), Protection of Stored Products (6), compulsory internships (6 CP in year 2 + 4 CP in year 3), free-choice credits (6 CP year 2 in Food Technology, 12 CP year 3 in both) and a 6 CP thesis. No dual-study four-year variant. Part-time enrolment is available as a general unibz option. The major is selected on entering the second year, not at application, so applicants apply to a single programme.
english_only_accessibility: effectively-closed for a candidate who knows ONLY English — but this is the LOWEST language bar of any unibz trilingual bachelor, so it is the most realistic trilingual programme for an international applicant. Entry requires B2 in the 1st language AND B1 in the 2nd language ('Preference will be given to candidates with a B2 level in their 2nd language'); a candidate who can certify only English can certify only one language and is excluded from the admission procedure, not merely ranked lower. The concrete minimum for a Turkish applicant is therefore English B2 + Italian OR German B1 — one CEFR step lower than the B2/B2 demanded by, for example, the Bachelor in Computer Science. The ranking-list decree words the criterion as B2 in at least two of the three teaching languages, adding 'in caso di posti disponibili l'ammissione è possibile anche con livello B1' (where places remain, admission is also possible with B1). EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE that the gate is passable: in the 2026/27 Early Bird session 1 non-EU applicant living abroad WAS admitted (score 13.78/15) while 5 non-EU applicants were excluded on language, and 27 EU/equivalent were admitted with 5 excluded on language; three applicants excluded in the Early Bird session (IDs 148850, 152198, 152910) re-applied in the Late session and were admitted, showing the language gap can be closed between sessions. Beyond admission, the programme is genuinely not English-taught: German appears in 20 CP of the compulsory first year and Italian dominates year 2, and graduation requires C1/B2/B2 across all three languages.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato / limited places) with a merit-based ranking list. There is NO entrance exam, no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT, no interview, no portfolio and no motivation letter. Selection is a purely documentary evaluation of upper-secondary-school grades (max 15 points) by a Faculty admission commission, preceded by an eliminatory language-eligibility gate (B2 in the 1st language + B1 in the 2nd). Separate ranking lists are drawn up for (a) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (b) non-EU citizens living abroad. OFA (additional learning obligations) in Mathematics and/or Chemistry are assigned within the same procedure.
academic_requirements: Required qualification (one of): (a) a secondary school leaving certificate of the Italian system; or (b) an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign school-leaving certificate counts as equivalent only if obtained after 12 years of education AND the applicant attended at least the last two years in that foreign school system (stated example: an Irish Leaving Certificate obtained after only one year is not sufficient). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research sets additional specific requirements for holders of certain certificates — American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates are named explicitly; those applicants should contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service). Beyond the title, the programme requires 'an adequate initial preparation in mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology', verified through school records; an incomplete preparation does not exclude the candidate but triggers OFA. Language requirements (1st language B2, 2nd language B1) are a separate, eliminatory condition. No ECTS/SSD credit requirements apply (bachelor level). National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 study programmes is allowed provided they do not belong to the same class and differ in at least 2/3 of course contents.
entry_exam_or_test: NONE. No unibz admission exam, no TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT and no subject test. The only examinations connected with admission are LANGUAGE exams at the unibz Language Centre, and only for applicants who choose that route of proof: Early Bird session — 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late session — 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). For this programme B1 AND B2 level exams can be registered for (unlike programmes requiring B2/B2, where only B2 exams are available), but only one level per language per session. Separately, AFTER admission there are non-selective instruments: a specific OFA exam in Mathematics and/or Chemistry (with catch-up courses and a Mathematics pre-course 21/09-09/10/2026), and a third-language placement test for admitted students who cannot certify their third language.
selection_scoring: Documentary scoring by the Faculty admission commission, maximum 15 points: up to 5 points for the average of the grades obtained in the third-last and penultimate year of upper secondary school (grades in behaviour, religion and physical education are excluded); up to 5 points for the average of the MATHEMATICS grades; up to 5 points for the average of the BIOLOGY, PHYSICS and CHEMISTRY grades. Grades are self-certified in the application portal; applicants who completed those years abroad must upload the report cards (with official translation into Italian, German or English if needed) and, for foreign schools, the complete grading scale indicating the pass mark. If the applicant fails to indicate the final grades of a year, the commission assigns that year the PASS MARK — a real scoring penalty rather than an exclusion. For candidates from school systems that differ substantially from the Italian one and that have no third-last/penultimate-year report cards, the commission may evaluate report cards from other school years. Tie-break: priority to the YOUNGEST candidate. No published minimum passing score. Competition in 2026/27 was very low: the Early Bird EU list admitted 27 people with scores from 14.45 down to 3.00/15, and the Late EU list admitted 22 with scores from 14.79 down to 2.42/15 — in practice every language-eligible applicant was admitted, so the binding constraints are the language gate and the deadline, not the score.
bonus_points: NONE. The scoring rubric is closed at 15 points across three grade averages. There is no extracurricular-experience bonus (unlike the Bachelor in Computer Science), no Webometrics university-ranking bonus, no GMAT/GRE bonus and no start-up-project bonus. The only preference mechanisms in the procedure are (a) the stated preference for candidates holding B2 rather than B1 in their second language, and (b) the age tie-break in favour of the younger candidate. Separately, for the Municipality of Meran-Merano scholarship (post-enrolment, not admission), residence in the municipality of Meran-Merano gives priority in the scholarship ranking and one extra point is awarded for each exam passed 'with honours' (30 e lode).
portfolio_and_materials: No portfolio, no motivation letter, no video, no project proposal, no reference letters and no CV are required. There are no file-size or page limits to record because no portfolio-type materials exist for this programme. The only substantive upload beyond identity and school documents is the self-certified table of subjects and final grades for the third-last and penultimate school year, entered directly in the application portal, plus scanned report cards (and official translations into Italian, German or English) for years completed abroad. Documentation relating to the school curriculum may be submitted in any of the three teaching languages. Candidates must upload the required documents by the application deadline 'under penalty of automatic exclusion from the process'; once submitted, the application cannot be modified.
interview: No interview. The admission procedure is entirely documentary and no interview dates are published for this programme. The only scheduled applicant-facing event is a non-selective Online Info Session on Thursday 3 September 2026, 17:00 CEST, at which professors and current students answer questions.
conditional_admission: Applicants still in their final year of upper secondary school apply and are ranked on the basis of third-last and penultimate year grades, so applying before graduation is the normal case rather than a special regime; the diploma is uploaded at enrolment ('if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment'). Holders of a foreign qualification are admitted with reserve: unibz performs its own checks and 'reserves the right to request additional documents', and an applicant who turns out not to possess a valid admission qualification 'can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment'. Non-EU applicants living abroad are additionally admitted with reserve until the Italian consulate in their country sends official confirmation directly to unibz. Refund rule tied to this: fees paid to secure a place are non-refundable except if the applicant fails the secondary-school final exam (maturità) or, for non-EU applicants living abroad, does not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities. [uncertain] — the ≥120/140 ECTS conditional-admission threshold and the 11/12/2026 late-enrolment window in the field schema are MASTER-level rules and do not apply to this bachelor programme.
ofa_rules: OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) applies in TWO separate subject areas, which is unusual — most unibz programmes assign only one. Adequate initial preparation in mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology is required and is verified through school records. Thresholds: to be admitted WITHOUT OFA a candidate must score MORE than 3 points out of 5 in the mathematics average AND more than 3 points out of 5 in the biology/physics/chemistry average. Consequently: 3 points or less on the mathematics average → OFA in MATHEMATICS; 3 points or less on the biology/physics/chemistry average → OFA in CHEMISTRY. A candidate can carry both. OFA are fulfilled by passing a specific exam; the Faculty offers additional catch-up courses reviewing basic mathematics and/or chemistry concepts, and a Mathematics pre-course runs 21/09-09/10/2026. Consequence of non-completion: a student who does not fulfil the OFA within the first year may enrol in the second year but CANNOT take any second- or third-year exams. Note this is a grade-based OFA (like Computer Science), not a test-based OFA as in the economics programmes.
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and the language rule is eliminatory: failing it means exclusion from the admission procedure, not a lower rank. ENTRY: 1st language B2, 2nd language B1, 3rd language no level required — with the explicit note 'Preference will be given to candidates with a B2 level in their 2nd language'. EXIT (to graduate): 1st language C1, 2nd language B2, 3rd language B2. Language positions are defined by the applicant's own proficiency, not by which language it is: the 1st language is the one in which the applicant is strongest (B2 or C1), the 3rd the weakest, possibly absolute beginner. Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and recommended (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd. A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations held in that language — a real constraint here, because the compulsory first year contains 20 CP of German and 6 CP of Italian courses alongside 37 CP of English ones, so a student cannot avoid sitting exams in at least two languages. Admitted students who cannot certify the third language take a placement test (details by e-mail) and are assigned a learning path aiming at B2 'as soon as possible'. Language Centre courses are free: extensive courses 4 h/week during semesters, intensive courses 8 h/week between semesters, and a three-week pre-semester intensive session 01-18/09/2026 (Mon-Fri, 6 h/day). A1 beginner courses are offered ONLY in that September pre-semester session and no longer during the academic year, so absolute beginners must start there. Target levels in the third language: B1 by the end of year 1, B2 by the end of year 2.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: B2 — 2nd language: B1 (B2 preferred) — 3rd language: no level required. This 'B2/B1/none' pattern is the most permissive entry profile among unibz trilingual programmes: compare B2/B2/none (Computer Science, Electronic and Information Engineering) and C1/B2/none (Public Policy, Accounting and Finance). Position is set by the candidate's own strength ranking, not by which language it is. Because a B1 second language is admissible, applicants for this programme may register at the unibz Language Centre for BOTH B1 and B2 level exams (only one level per language per session), whereas B2/B2 programmes allow B2 registrations only. The signed ranking-list decrees state the rule as B2 in at least two of the three teaching languages with the qualifier that, where places remain available, admission is also possible at B1 — consistent with the B2 preference wording in the admission-information document.
exit_levels: To graduate: 1st language C1, 2nd language B2, 3rd language B2 (CEFR). This is one step easier in the second language than the standard unibz C1/C1/B2 trilingual exit profile, but it is still a real graduation gate: a student admitted at B2/B1/none must raise the first language to C1, the second from B1 to B2, and go from zero to B2 in the third language within three years. Free Language Centre courses are structured to support this (third language: B1 by end of year 1, B2 by end of year 2).
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations held in that language. There is no programme-specific mid-January English deadline of the kind applied to the Bachelor in Computer Science, because the first semester of this programme is NOT English-only — year 1 mixes English (37 CP), German (20 CP) and Italian (6 CP) courses. The practical consequence is that a student whose third language is German or Italian must reach B1 in it quickly to avoid being blocked from a substantial share of first- and second-year exams (German carries 20 CP already in year 1; Italian carries 30 CP in year 2 in both majors).
proof_pathways: Four recognised pathways: (1) the main teaching language of the final high-school year, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1 (Ladin upper secondary schools: recognised as B2 in German and Italian); for foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not clearly stated on the diploma, a letter or document from the high school stating it must also be uploaded. (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English — recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload their certificates and/or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); foreign degrees need a university letter stating the medium of instruction if not on the degree. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list; if it cannot be uploaded it may be sent by e-mail as a PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) Language exams organised by the unibz Language Centre, registered online in the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application — Early Bird: 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late: 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026); for this programme both B1 and B2 exams may be taken, but only one level per language per session. Additional route for foreign and bi-/multilingual schools: if CEFR levels for German, Italian or English are explicitly stated on the graduation diploma and all four skills (reading, listening, speaking, writing) were assessed, those levels are accepted as proof for the 2nd and/or 3rd language, subject to Language Centre approval. Administrative detail: a final certificate awarded by an Italian public institution requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original diploma.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants'). Rules: (1) the certificate must assess ALL FOUR skills and be issued by the certification organisation itself; (2) it must show adequate performance in all skills as an overall grade, or the detailed assessment must appear on the certificate or in appropriate documentation from the issuer; (3) if no overall result or level is stated, THE LOWEST LEVEL REACHED IN ANY SUB-SKILL determines the recognised level, provided that part was passed; (4) there is NO COMPENSATION for failed exam parts and no averages are calculated unless the certification organisation itself provides them; (5) certificates obtained through an online 'home edition' exam are NOT recognised, except those explicitly flagged in the list; (6) certificates covering single skills issued by different organisations are not accepted; (7) certificates of participation, end-of-course tests and exams from private educational institutions, and placement-test results are not recognised; (8) certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff are not recognised; (9) DAAD certificates are NOT recognised. Validity: international language certificates must not be older than FIVE YEARS at the date of submission, counting the entire calendar year from 1 January. Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf
application_deadline_eu: Three sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO normalised below). Early Bird Application: 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. Late Application (EU only): 28/05/2026 - 08/07/2026 by noon local time = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08. Additional Application Session (EU only, opened by the Faculty in August/September if places remain — and it WAS opened for this programme in 2026/27): 18/08/2026 - 04/09/2026 by noon local time = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04. EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and an applicant excluded in one session may apply again in the next — three Early Bird rejects did exactly that and were admitted in the Late session.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the Early Bird Application, 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are NOT eligible for the Late Application or the Additional Application Session, pay a non-refundable €50 application fee, are ranked on a separate list against a separate 4-place quota, and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) for the study visa. For academic year 2026/27 this window is closed; the next opportunity for a non-EU applicant living abroad is the 2027/28 Early Bird session (expected around March-April 2027).
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU applicants — the critical third category for Turkish applicants: (1) citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; (2) non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian permit to stay ('permesso di soggiorno') under article 39 paragraph 5 of Legislative Decree no. 286 of 25/07/1998 — for WORK, FAMILY reasons, POLITICAL or HUMANITARIAN ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS reasons. Such applicants apply directly to the University and must upload a copy of the valid permit; if it has expired, a renewal request must be attached. A permit to stay for STUDY reasons or a tourist visa is NOT sufficient. Critical warning: 'if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin' — losing access to the Late and Additional sessions, to the 50-place EU quota, and being pushed onto the 4-place non-EU list. For this programme in 2026/27 that distinction was decisive: the parity route led to a session (the Additional one, 18/08-04/09/2026) that is still open, whereas the non-EU-abroad route closed on 28/04/2026.
places_quotas: Three separate quotas for 2026/27, all confirmed by the admission-information document. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: Early Bird Application 40 places, Late Application 10 places — summarised on the programme page and brochure as 'Places available: 50 EU + 4 Non-EU'. Non-EU citizens living abroad: Early Bird Application 4 places, and no non-EU quota in any later session. Carry-over rule (EU/equivalent only): 'any remaining places of the early bird application will be offered in the late application'. ACTUAL 2026/27 UPTAKE: Early Bird — 27 EU/equivalent admitted against 40 places (5 EU applicants excluded for failing the language requirements) and 1 non-EU applicant admitted against 4 places (5 non-EU applicants excluded for language). Late — 22 EU/equivalent admitted (13 Early Bird carry-over places + 10 Late places = 23 available). Cumulative EU/equivalent admissions 49 against the 50-place EU quota, which is why the Faculty then opened the Additional Application Session. Non-EU places were left substantially unfilled (1 of 4).
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: Early Bird: ranking lists published by 27/05/2026 (the signed EU + non-EU decree was produced on 15/05/2026); payment of the 1st instalment of tuition fees (€600 — this is what secures the place) by 05/06/2026 noon; enrolment from 10/07/2026 to 06/08/2026 noon. Late Application: ranking lists by 30/07/2026 (decree produced 17/07/2026); 1st instalment by 06/08/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 06/08/2026 noon. Additional Application Session: ranking lists by 18/09/2026; 1st instalment by 25/09/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 25/09/2026 noon. Missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the place passes to the next applicant on the list. An applicant admitted to more than one programme may secure up to 2 places by paying the instalment twice. Paying does NOT confer student status — only enrolment does — and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol (exceptions: failing the maturità, or, for non-EU applicants abroad, not obtaining the documents from the Italian authorities). The signed ranking decrees carry the standard 60-day right of appeal to the Administrative Court of Bolzano. [uncertain] — the ranking PDFs print 'Bolzano, data della firma' instead of a typed date; the dates given here are the PDF creation dates (15/05/2026 and 17/07/2026), which precede the published-by deadlines.
programme_specific_dates: Preparatory and start-of-year dates for 2026/27: intensive language courses 01-18/09/2026 (Mon-Fri, 6 h/day); MATHEMATICS PRE-COURSE 21/09-09/10/2026 (programme-specific, tied to the Mathematics OFA); Freshers Days 28-29/09/2026. Online Info Session for prospective students: Thursday 3 September 2026, 17:00 CEST (registration via the programme page) — note this falls one day BEFORE the Additional Application Session deadline of 04/09/2026. Academic calendar: 1st semester classes 28/09-23/12/2026, extraordinary exam session 10-23/12/2026, holidays 24/12/2026-06/01/2027, classes 07-23/01/2027, exams 25/01-20/02/2027; 2nd semester classes 01/03-25/03/2027, holidays 26-29/03/2027, classes 30/03-12/06/2027, extraordinary exam session 12-22/05/2027, exams 14/06-10/07/2027; autumn exam session 23/08-25/09/2027. Admission-linked programme dates are limited to the Language Centre exam sessions (16/03/2026; 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026; 22-26/06/2026) — there are no entrance-exam, interview or portfolio-submission dates because none of those instruments are used. Third-language placement test: date communicated by e-mail to admitted students. Scholarship date (post-enrolment): the Municipality of Meran-Merano call for the 2025 cohort closed 21/07/2026 at 12:00 with payment by 30/09/2026.
required_documents: At application (online via https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; the completed online form; self-certified subjects and final grades for the third-last and penultimate year of upper secondary school; for years completed abroad, scanned copies of the relevant report cards plus, for foreign schools, the complete grading scale indicating the pass mark; official translations of the report cards into Italian, German or English where necessary; language certificates uploaded under 'upload language certificates' (mandatory for the 1st and 2nd language, recommended for the 3rd) and/or registration for Language Centre exams; the diploma of the qualification if already obtained abroad; for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay (plus renewal request if expired). NOTE: there is NO 'study career' Excel template for this programme — that structured upload is a master-level requirement. At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must additionally upload the secondary school diploma; an official translation into Italian (not needed for diplomas issued in German or English); and the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. Once submitted the application cannot be modified, and forms filled in but not correctly sent are disregarded. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. Students transferring from another Italian university must give the Student Office a copy of the transfer application at the start of the academic year; non-EU students must hand in a copy of the residence permit once obtained.
application_fee: €50, payable only by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. It is described as an administration fee and is explicitly NON-REFUNDABLE. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay for work, family, asylum or religious reasons) pay no application fee.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total tuition fees are €1,200 per year in two instalments: 1st instalment €600 (including the €16 revenue stamp / marca da bollo) — this is the payment that secures the place after admission; 2nd instalment €600, due by March of the following year. Late payment of the second instalment incurs a fine; unpaid fees block exam-taking and any transfer to another university or study programme. No refund if you drop out, interrupt your studies or are excluded. Exemptions: students with a disability recognised under article 3 paragraph 1 of Law no. 104/1992 or with a disability of 66% or more (health-authority certificate to be handed in at the start of the academic year), and foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Students awarded a scholarship by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to a refund of the tuition fees. Fees pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ and the programme's own admission-information PDF: https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/bachelor-in-food-and-enogastronomy-sciences_admission-information_en_GB.pdf
scholarships_grants: PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC (unique to this degree at unibz): the Municipality of Meran-Merano awards FIVE scholarships of €1,000 gross each to students enrolled in the FIRST YEAR of this programme, under an agreement between the municipality and the Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences. The programme page and brochure announce the 2026/27 round and state that four of the five are reserved for students resident in the municipality of Meran-Merano, with unclaimed reserved scholarships falling back to the general ranking. The only call actually published so far is the one for the 2025 cohort (students in their first year in 2025/26): applications by e-mail to didactic.agriculture@unibz.it using the attached form by 21/07/2026 12:00; commission Prof. Emanuele Boselli (chair), Prof. Giovanna Ferrentino, Dr Massimiliano Calvia; criteria max 50 points for total credits earned by the summer exam session + max 50 points for the weighted grade average (max 30/30) + 1 extra point per exam passed 'with honours'; minimum 40 points to enter the ranking; residents of the Municipality of Meran-Merano have PRIORITY in the ranking; tie-break to the younger candidate; acceptance within 7 working days by e-mail; single payment by 30/09/2026; taxed as a scholarship under art. 50(1)(c) TUIR. IMPORTANT: this is a post-enrolment merit award, not an admission scholarship, and it is not means-tested. GENERAL ROUTE: the income-based provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano (ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and grants fostering postgraduate studies), applied for online through the provincial e-government service with help from the South Tyrolean Students Association; grant holders also get a refund of tuition fees. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' — a newly arrived non-EU first-year student is effectively ineligible in year one, which makes the €1,000 Meran-Merano award the only realistic first-year cash support. Other listed sources: Italian government grants, Austrian and German (BAföG) grants, DAAD summer-course scholarships, loans from Italian banks. Contact: study@unibz.it, +39 0471 012900. [uncertain] — the frequently quoted provincial range of roughly €1,680-€6,960 per year and any merit threshold such as a 27/30 average could not be confirmed on the pages verified for this programme; amounts are set annually by the provincial call. credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must upload the diploma plus an official translation into Italian (not required for diplomas issued in German or English), and then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate — a Statement of Correspondence of the secondary school diploma, downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database Italy, https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that ARE signatories to the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA; (c) non-EU countries that are NOT signatories of the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Türkiye is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification. unibz performs its own checks on the foreign qualification and reserves the right to request additional documents in case of doubt; a candidate found not to possess a valid admission qualification can be excluded by Rector's decree even after enrolment. For the admission scoring, foreign applicants must also supply the complete grading scale of their school with the pass mark indicated, so that the commission can convert grade averages. Signatory list: https://www.enic-naric.net/ ; CIMEA services: https://cimea-diplome.it/ . Recognition of credit points from previous university studies is possible only after enrolment and only where the exams taken elsewhere are equivalent in content to unibz courses.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window only (€50 non-refundable fee) → appear on the separate non-EU ranking list (4 places) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by the published deadline → THEN pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (https://www.universitaly.it/). The Universitaly application is MANDATORY — 'otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol' — and only ONE study programme may be selected there. The Italian diplomatic authorities in the applicant's country then issue the study/university entry visa. Programme-specific nuance: non-EU applicants living abroad are admitted WITH RESERVE, and the reserve is lifted only when the Italian consulate abroad sends official confirmation directly to unibz. unibz warns that admission does not automatically confer any right to obtain a visa. Financial means for the visa: at least €800 per month for living costs (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing) excluding tuition fees; total proof of at least €36,000 for a bachelor programme (€24,000 for a master); health insurance and visa expenses on top. After arrival: the residence permit ('permesso di soggiorno') must be APPLIED FOR within 8 working days of arrival in Italy — contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival — and once obtained a copy must be handed in to the Student Office in person or by e-mail. Student work is limited to no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities are entitled to a refund. Reference page: https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/international/international-degree-seeking-applicants/degree-seeking-non-eu-citizens-living-abroad/

uncertainty_notes: Data year: all figures are for academic year 2026/27; the admission-information PDF carries 'Latest update: 19.08.2026' and the express caveat 'Subject to change'. Verified 2026-08-29. TIME-CRITICAL: the Early Bird and Late sessions for 2026/27 are closed and their ranking lists are published, but the Additional Application Session (18/08-04/09/2026, EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only) is OPEN at the verification date and closes at noon on 04/09/2026 — six days later. (1) Teaching-language weighting is reconstructed from the per-module tags in the L-26 course-description PDF dated 01.02.2025 combined with the brochure study plans; one module is tagged '3 credits EN' in the course description but 6 CP in the brochure (Sustainable cultivation methods and quality of products for food processing), so the English total may be 3 CP lower than stated. Free-choice credits, internships and the thesis carry no fixed language and are excluded from the per-language totals. (2) Programme history: the identification of this degree as a renamed and restructured continuation of the 'Bachelor in Enogastronomy in Mountain Areas' (announced 22/03/2022) is inferred from the legacy URL redirect, the surviving 'course offering 2022' page for students 'Enrolled before 2025', and the 'coorte 2025' wording of the scholarship call — unibz does not state the rename in English. (3) Meran-Merano scholarship: the only published call is for the 2025 cohort (deadline 21/07/2026, already passed); the 2026/27 round is announced on the programme page but no call document was published at the verification date, and the two texts differ on whether four scholarships are RESERVED for Meran-Merano residents or residents merely have PRIORITY in the ranking. (4) The ranking-list PDFs print 'Bolzano, data della firma' rather than a typed date; the dates cited (15/05/2026 Early Bird, 17/07/2026 Late) are PDF creation timestamps, not the certified signature dates. (5) In the Early Bird EU list, positions 22-27 are printed out of score order (6.85, then 13.92, 13.00, 8.65, 5.95, 3.00), suggesting a second batch appended to the decree; the admitted count of 27 is stated in words and is reliable, the internal ordering less so. (6) Provincial study-grant amounts are not confirmed for 2026/27; the €1,680-€6,960 range in the field schema comes from secondary summaries and could not be verified on any page checked for this programme. (7) No separate call/manifesto exists in English; the Faculty 'regolamento di ammissione' referenced by the ranking decrees was not located at a public URL. (8) No 'study career' Excel template and no bachelor-level ECTS conditional-admission threshold apply here — both are master-level instruments. (9) Turkish-applicant relevance: Türkiye's status as a Lisbon Convention signatory (hence case (b) recognition: ARDI + CIMEA verification) is inferred from convention membership, not stated by unibz for this programme. (10) Campus: 'Bozen-Bolzano' is the official designation; the additional use of NOI Techpark laboratories and the Merano workshop venues comes from the 2022 launch news item and the programme page photo captions, not from a formal location statement, so day-to-day teaching may be split across sites.
